utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, after the discussion we had yesterday about a document which I wanted to produce, I should like to say that the Prosecutor envisages to bring back the witness Morsink because he was the one who turned the document over to the Prosecutor. I should like also to make it clear that this was an annex to the statement of Mr. Morsink, which was communicated to the Defence on the 5th of March last year under the obligation that we have. If this was not introduced through Mr. Morsink; that is, on the 8th of October when this large batch of documents was sent. This document was turned over to the Prosecution on the 16th of December last year, among a number of documents which the Prosecutor intends to produce in this case still. As for the testimony of Mr. Morsink, if it does take place, it is quite clear that Mr. Morsink will be able to tell us about the document, notably about its source, because he will know who gave him the document. As for the authenticity of the document, that is another matter which I wish to mention. It seems to me that it is necessary to insist on the fact that the authenticity of the document, at least as the dictionary would say, does not mean that the quality of the document and the source of the person to whom it is attributed, but also it means that the document is truthful that is, that it corresponds to the truth. And I should say, therefore, not only in the strictest sense -- it is authentic not only in the strictest sense of the word, that is, as to the source of the document, but also that it contains facts, true facts. I should also like to say that the second question that was raised yesterday will not arise, because the document was already produced here in the court by another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, the Chamber will have something to say about this in a moment, but let us now complete the evidence of this witness, and at a suitable moment during the day we can mention possible ways of dealing with it. Yes. We have got, I think, to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Lopez-Terres:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AC, in the cinema, as you told us yesterday, with several hundred other prisoners. On the 5th of May, 1993, you were in the cinema, and from that cinema you were transferred with other persons such as Mr. Kaknjo, Mr. Batija Sivro, Kadir Dzidic, Edib Zlotrg, and Enes Surkovic to the chess club and then to Kaonik near Busovaca, and that was after the order was issued by General Petkovic to release all the prisoners. We shall resume at this point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I should like to say two things. First, I said there was a larger number of prisoners. There were over 500 detainees. Secondly, the release of all prisoners was concluded earlier. And after that we were taken to the chess club, with the clear intention to then surreptitiously to be transferred to Kaonik, because in addition to me there were 12 very prominent men in the group that I was in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay in the Kaonik camp, which lasted until the 14th, or the 15th of May, 1993, did you get there some information?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see there is an objection, even though I have not finished my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's hear the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, we have reached the paragraph 58, and I should like to repeat my objection, which is the same as with regard to the paragraph that I mentioned yesterday. That is, here we see how they arrived at the conclusion. We do not see the ground for the conclusion, and the only thing we see here is the conclusion, rather than the facts. So the objection is identical to the ones that I raised yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, if you'd like to lay the foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AC, did you have any information about the source of the decision that was taken to take you to Kaonik from Vitez at the time when you were to be freed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: We were secretly transferred by the members of the HVO military police. And the source, the origin of decision is quite clear, because it is indicative of the responsibility of the military police in this system of decision-making and the whole hierarchical structure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know from whom did this military police receive the instructions to transfer you to Kaonik? Secondly, from whom did Kaonik receive instructions to set you free?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: We got that information during our stay in Kaonik, where one Marko -- that is what other HVO members in the camp called him -- said that Dario Kordic was behind our transfer to Kaonik, and that we would possibly be released or exchanged if Dario Kordic approved such a move.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was following authorisation with a guard of the camp that you and other detainees received that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during your detention in Kaonik, you were subjected to questioning but not to any threats, and you were not harassed, you were not ill-treated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the other hand, you could see that your fellow detainee, (redacted), after an interview, returned with a bruised face and that his jacket and his shoes had been taken away.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, (redacted). When he came back he was all bruised and he was missing his shoes and parts of his clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were released from the Kaonik camp and taken back to the cinema in Vitez on the 14th or 15th of May with the rest of the group that you spoke about, and you stayed at least one night in the Vitez cinema before you were set free?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to refer to the document, Exhibit Z928. It was produced yesterday. Could it be shown to the witness. And I should like to comment on this document, if I may, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this document is dated the 10th of May, 1993. It is signed by Mr. Zlatko Aleksovski, who was the warden of the camp at Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We're not opposing the document, but it is not true that the document is signed. It's clearly stated on the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This document, as I recollect, was attached to Mr. McLeod's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, whether it's signed or not, the name at the bottom is "Zlatko Aleksovski." Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite. What I was trying to say with regard to the document is that it was already annexed to Mr. McLeod's report, and it was simply for practical convenience, because this was only an annex to the report; it was not a separate exhibit. And that is why we decided to give it the number now, Z928, but it has the general number of Mr. McLeod's report, which was filed under the number Z926.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it your name which appears on page 2 of this document under 70?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise some other names of persons who were detained in Kaonik at the same time as you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I recognise the names of the whole group that was with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us those names, quickly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Serif Causevic, Alija Besic, Ferim Besic, Cazim Ahmic, Enes Surkovic, Ramo Kaknjo, Suad Salkic, Batija Sivro, Edib Zlotrg, Kadir Dzidic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 16th of May, '93, you and the detainees that had been transferred from the Kaonik Camp were exchanged for some HVO soldiers in Vitez, that is, soldiers who had been captured by the Bosnia-Herzegovina army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the day of your liberation, on the 16th of May, '93, you were beaten severely by the military within the cinema compound -- within the cinema precincts. Could you tell us something about this act of violence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say hit me, because it means being hit once. I was beaten. I was struck repeatedly. Members of the military police, namely, who were in the lobby, who were on guard, as a matter of fact in the cinema, they called me to come out. Allegedly, they had something to tell me, to transmit some information. And when I came out into the lobby, they started beating me with some wooden and metal objects, whatever they could lay their hands on. This whole scene was observed by one of their commanders, Anto Kovac, nicknamed Zabac, who did nothing to stop them. If I may, I should also like to add the following. At the moment where we were to be released, I let know the mayor, Ivan Santic, about this incident. And he told me that he would report it to their superior, Mario Cerkez. But no steps were taken in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with permission of the Court, could we switch places and could I start with that witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Kovacic:

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Bozidar Kovacic, I am an attorney from Rijeka, and together with colleague Mr. Mikulicic I represent Mr. Cerkez. And I will have a few questions for you. We speak the same language, so we understand one another, but we must not forget that what we are saying is being interpreted simultaneously, so please make a short break between the questions and answers, so that the interpreters can follow. Also, should you not understand the question, or should I put it incorrectly, please let me know, so I can rephrase it. I think I can begin now. Let me ask you first a few questions linked to the meeting held in the premises of the Territorial Defence on the 19th of October, 1992, in the evening, which you testified about at length. Let us first establish who was present. Will you please confirm or deny the names I am going to give. On behalf of the HVO there was Ivica Santic and Mario Cerkez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On behalf of the war presidency, Fuad Kaknjo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Munib Kajmovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Muhamed Mujezinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sefkija Djidic and yourself. Those were the persons present at that meeting, all of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I think Sulejman Kalco should be mentioned too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other witnesses testified here, and nobody mentioned Kalco. Are you sure he was present, or do you think he was present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Among those that you mentioned that evening, at that meeting; yes, I am quite sure that he was there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us also make sure who was what. Ivica Santic was town mayor and president of the HVO government at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the civilian branch of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The civilian and the military were integrated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never mind. We'll come back to that. But his title was president of the HVO government in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Cerkez, in October 1992, was a member of the municipal staff of the HVO, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a prominent figure, as a member of all these various bodies; you were aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The immediate superior at the time of Cerkez was Marion Skopljak, president of the HVO staff; the chief of staff in Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. At the meeting, on behalf of the HVO, were those two persons, Cerkez and Santic. Who spoke on behalf of the HVO at that meeting? Santic is the superior. Was he the one conducting the dialogue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, he was superior by position, but the dialogue was conducted mostly by Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AC, I should like to show you what two witnesses said in reference to that meeting. And could we go into private session for a moment, as one of the witnesses had a pseudonym, so as to avoid any error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What's the point, before you do, Mr. Kovacic, of asking the witness what somebody else said? All you are going to be doing is asking the witness to comment on what another witness has said. Now, if you want to make that sort of comment, of course you can make it to us, if there is some point of difference in this witness's evidence in relation to the other witnesses. But there really isn't any point, is there, in having him comment on what somebody else said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I wasn't going to ask him to comment. I just wished to show the witness that two of his colleagues, honourable men, testified in a quite a different manner, and I wanted to read him one of the answers from those testimonies. And this might refresh the memory of the witness. And then we would go on to the next issue: who made the phone call. Because I don't think it is immaterial whether Cerkez represented the HVO at the meeting or if he was escorting Mr. Santic. In my view, this is a substantial difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It is a difference we'll have to consider. This witness says one thing; other witnesses say something different. All that you would be doing by reading out what others said is to, in effect, have him comment on what they said. That's what you're going to do. Now, the people to make the comment to is the Court. You can say to us, in due course, "This is what X and C said and this is what Z said." You can ask the witness, if you want -- you could put to the witness, if you say he is mistaken, that other witnesses have said something else; does that make him change his mind about his evidence? You can put it like that. If you want to put the names of the witnesses, you can do so, and we will go into closed session, but you can't put the entire statement to him. You can just put it in summary form as a question. Do you want to go into closed session, Mr. Kovacic, to do it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would appreciate that, but it won't take more than one sentence just to refresh the witness's memory, and he might even change his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, until we go into closed session, Witness, you agree, I hope, with the statement that your colleagues -- are we in private session? Closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I said too much about earlier duties. Could identify the witness. But I think we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It can be redacted. If it was not in closed session, it can be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, you were involved in the economy. Tell me, from your personal experience, when you go to attend a business meeting with your own manager, your superior, at that meeting who is the main interlocutor with a third party, your superior or someone lower down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It depends what issues are discussed. If there are issues within my terms of reference, obviously I would be responsible. Otherwise, why would I be going to the meeting?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but only if your general manager asks you to enter into a dialogue on those issues.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It could be like that, but it need not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Similarly, if you go to a business meeting and take a subordinate, because of his specialised knowledge, to that meeting, who would be the speaker, you or your younger assistant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I would repeat the same answer that I gave a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Please, your allegation that you made a moment ago, it is based on what? And after you told us that you were familiar with the situation and that Cerkez was in the municipal staff of the HVO at the time and that his immediate superior was Marijan Skopljak at the time, on which grounds do you allege that Kordic was Cerkez's boss or commander? That's what you said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I said that that was what the accused Cerkez told us explicitly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He told you that Kordic was his superior. And you have no other basis for that statement? Do you have anybody else's statement to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I think that all the Croats in the Lasva Valley saw the accused Dario Kordic as the military and political leader or chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I assume that we would agree that you're not trying to say that Kordic is the immediate superior of Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I didn't even say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your allegation that Kordic was Cerkez's commander does not mean that he was his immediate commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I said that the accused Cerkez said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he didn't say that he was his immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: He didn't need to explain to us their relationship.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, let us clarify a little the reason for the meeting. The mentioned persons, Santic and Cerkez, came to the meeting in the quest for a solution to the problem, the problem being the roadblock at Ahmici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No solution can be achieved by ultimatums.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you give me a precise answer, please? The topic of discussion at the meeting was to find a way to remove the barricade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: What they were really interested in -- that is, Santic and Cerkez -- was not the physical removal of the roadblock but the passage of their units to Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. On the other hand, you, the people of Vitez, both sides, the citizens of Vitez who were attending the meeting, it was in your interest. If certain troops needed to pass through Vitez, it was in your interest to make sure that the troops pass through Vitez and that they don't stay on there. That was your prime concern, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. That simply is not correct, because the troops were supposed to come from Busovaca, through Vitez, and go on to Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't agree that it was in the interest of the local people, and I'm thinking of representatives of both communities, for them just to pass through rather than to be stationed in your town? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I could agree with that. Since -- if we hadn't known where those troops were going, and they were really going to reinforce HVO troops in Novi Travnik, where tensions were already very high.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I will have to tell you once again that a co-participant from that meeting, who testified here under the pseudonym L, explicitly said that the gist of the matter was to find a solution how these "outside troops" should pass through Vitez and not stay on in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Certainly that was one of the concerns and part of the solution, but the way chosen by Santic and Cerkez was to issue an ultimatum to explicitly demand the removal of the barricade and free passage for their units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Santic and Cerkez, or anyone else, did not say that those troops had to go through Vitez, and that was why they were requesting the lifting of the barricade so as to go on to Novi Travnik. They were saying something else. But it was your side which inferred that it was Novi Travnik that they were headed for.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It wasn't only our inference, but the telephone conversation also confirmed that. They accused Dario Kordic, who was in Novi Travnik already, was requesting that the unit be allowed to move on to Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if they go to Jajce, they have to use the same route?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In a way, yes, but the Croat side never mentioned anything of the kind. And, listen, what I should like to say now is that both sides were aware that if the roadblock were not lifted, that it could entail, it could result in an armed conflict. And somebody who was said to go to Jajce, I think would realise that and try to avoid a conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I am asking you to answer a very simple question. Did the negotiating parties, that is Cerkez and Santic, tell you that they were asking for the removal of the roadblocks so that the HVO troops coming from other municipalities move onto Novi Travnik; or was it the conclusion that you arrived at, that, in fact, they wanted to go to Novi Travnik? Very simple.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: We also arrived at that conclusion, but the course of the meeting and the conversation with Kordic confirmed this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was subsequently when the conversation took place, but Cerkez and Santic did not say that the troops were headed for Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: They said that the troops had to go through, but they -- neither did they say that they were headed for Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But you will agree that it is beyond dispute that at the time the HVO and the BiH army were fighting side by side to defend Jajce against the Serb troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, but the circumstances of it were very strange indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I have reasons to believe that you know that. That same evening other meetings took place, and several, or I should say quite a number of bilateral contacts were established in search of a peaceful solution. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I don't know what meetings you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, for instance, there was a meeting at the health centre about one hour later, according to the information that we have.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: But I was in these premises --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, right. You told us all of that. Excuse me for interrupting you. But my question is: Do you know that other meetings, or at least one other meeting, was held, and several bilateral conversations took place between those eminent personalities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, you would have to define the term "eminent personalities," because, after all, this was the meeting that was trying to resolve this question in a fundamental manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'll ask you it a different way, then. Did you know, did you learn later on that evening, or some other time, that that same evening, another meeting or meetings were held which were also trying to find a peaceful solution to a potential conflict? Are you aware of that or not? Just that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not. Are you aware that that same evening there were several bilateral attempts by some important personalities, such as Santic, such as Kajmovic, such as Marijan Skopljak, who made various phone calls, trying to address information to the other side in trying to arrive at some solution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, the communication was not cut off. The links were not cut off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was a channel which could be used to devise some solution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a channel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. You keep insisting on that request to lift the roadblock. And let us try to save some time. And I shall suggest something to you and then you can confirm it or deny it. On the main road through the Lasva Valley, below the village of Ahmici, a military roadblock or a barricade was put up, and this roadblock was manned by infantry, by armed units of the BiH army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That roadblock was set up on the basis of orders which arrived from the 3rd Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I did not see that documentation of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you must have heard about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I think that a decision to set up the roadblock was taken by Sefkija Djidic, but it could be that other persons from the corps consented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean Sefkija Djidic, the local commander of the army of BiH in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that same day, on the other side of the approach to Vitez, but on the same road at Grbavica, next to the Bosna building enterprise, another roadblock was set up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That roadblock, if it existed, and I am not aware of that, but if it existed, it would be mostly symbolical and, militarily speaking, of lesser importance than the former one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. We can agree that it was very political and militarily less important, but it was set up nevertheless?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I never said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So, the negotiations failed. And the next morning, the HVO army attacked the roadblock; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The army attack was not directed at the village, even though some damage was caused to some facilities and houses in the immediate vicinity of the roadblock where the conflict took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct, because a large number of buildings, of structures around the roadblock, were attacked as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that conflict, unfortunately, there were casualties on both sides?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that it was Ivan Santic who led the attack? You were not there, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I was not there, but I said that my sister's husband, my brother-in-law, who lived in the immediate vicinity, had told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we just make a correction. Nenad Santic, not Ivan Santic. Nenad Santic. Do you remember when it was when he told you that, and where did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: He told me that sometime in early November, in my flat in Vitez, because we often visited one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please be good enough to give us his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, even if shots were fired at the minaret in Ahmici, the minaret did not topple, did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while we are talking about Nenad, let us finish what we have to say about him. Do you know that he lives about 100 metres from the roadblock?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I do not know the houses he lives in, but, yes, it is nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then you told us that after the roadblock was removed, that kind of a truce was signed then. And could the witness be shown the exhibit already tendered, Z2461. While we are waiting for the document, you will agree, won't you, that after this quite remarkable incident, this conflict, this clash between the two sides, all the politicians of that locality from both sides were trying to get together and devise some solution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Quite. The Bosnia side always wanted to find a solution, a peaceful solution, so as not to have -- to solve their problems in that particular manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 246,1. Point 1. Will you please also prepare D17/1-12 and -13. Will you please have a look at this document, especially at those present. The title -- will you please look at the contents. And my question is the following: Did you mean this document when you said that a kind of a truce was signed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the document that you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So there were present representatives of the UNHCR, UNPROFOR, and there were priests, representatives of clergy, both Muslim and Catholic; there were representatives of armed forces, political representatives. Mario Cerkez, evidently, came later, because his name is written by hand as representative of the municipal HVO headquarters. And it is quite evident that now a broad political effort is being made to try to calm things down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we agree about that. Thank you. Is it correct that after that, the municipality compensated for the damage to the houses and farm buildings which were around the roadblock and had been damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I learnt that some effort was made to compensate for part of the damage, but it was not compensated for in any noteworthy manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. These efforts -- and you told us that it was a time fraught with incidents, when Muslim shops were broken and the like. I should like to have document D17,1. And there are 12 and 13.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could those documents be placed on the ELMO, because the interpreters don't have them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, put the documents on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you please have a look at the document, the names there, the title, the signatories. Can we agree that, as for the subject matter, this is a document similar to the previous one? We see that the dialogue goes on, that these are some efforts to calm the situation in Vitez down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we agree about that. Do we agree that the signatories really held those posts which are mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now the next document, please, D17/1-13. Will you please take a look? So the first sentence of this letter and the last item in the previous document, we see that one of the conclusions reached by the preceding session is being put through; that is, the confiscated military equipment is exchanged, and that was the conclusion of item 4 of the earlier agreement. And Cerkez signs this letter, which he then sends it to Sefkija Dzidic, as the then deputy commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. Have you heard anything about this document? Do you know if these conclusions were put through, or at least the majority of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I don't know, because this was happening at the time when I had the visit of HVO members, that is, at the time when my family and I were ill-treated by the HVO in our flat. After that, for a short while I was absent from Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. But do you agree that this -- all this was part of the attempt to bring down the tension in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. On paper, yes, but the situation on the ground, especially when it comes to the HVO behaviour, did not lead to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean that the situation in Vitez was not calmed down, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Quite true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. We'll go back to this issue briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, we're taking up some time. Now, the witness doesn't seem to be able to help very much about these matters. Can we move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going on to new topics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, in your testimony, you used the term "HVO" several times. A moment ago we agreed that this was a civilian and a military branch of the HVO. There was a civilian government in the Vitez municipality, and there's the military structure within the territory of the municipality. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, there were those two elements, but they acted in synchronisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume you will agree with me when I say that the HVO was the government of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. At the level of the municipality and elsewhere they had these two main elements. In the military structure of the HVO the situation changed as the situation developed, but let me ask you a few questions about that. Did you know that the Operational Zone of Central Bosnia was based in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the headquarters were in the hotel and everyone referred to it as the "Blaskic command"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that at the end of 1992 and until the middle of March 1993, there was a joint inter-municipal brigade, Vitez-Novi Travnik, known as Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the 1st Battalion of that brigade was based in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: One of those battalions. I don't know exactly the names, but one of them was based in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your earlier testimony, you mentioned the so-called special purpose unit Vitezovi. Did they exist within the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned the military police. Did that exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apropos the military police, it was based in the hotel, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1993 it was in the hotel too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, as a separate unit within the military police there was the special purpose unit the Jokers; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in December and January, there were units that people referred to as the Hercegovci, the Herzegovinians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. There were certain troops coming from that part of the country, so people referred to them in that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then there was a unit known as Ludvig Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: You mean in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Perhaps there were members of that unit, but I'm not familiar with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us summarise then. So we can agree that there were several different units all belonging to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Each of those units, by nature of things, by definition, has its own commander, structure, organisation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It has a micro-organisation, yes, but they also complied with orders coming from the supreme command in the region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we refer to all of them together as the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that for you, as a citizen, when two bandits come to your house and you consider them to be the HVO but, in fact, you don't care whom they belong to, all you need to know is that they were HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. That is sufficient and that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But regarding those two bandits who mistreated you for a whole hour in your own apartment, let me ask you: They wore no insignia, you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: They did not have any insignia, but other HVO members were waiting for them at the entrance to the flat, who didn't come in. And as soon as they left, I saw them from my window and I could see that they were members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't know which unit of the HVO they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then let me ask you, to finish with that incident, a most unfortunate and tragic incident for you, you were living in a building where the Benc cafe was and another 070 cafe.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: You mean the building where the Benc cafe is? No, not the same building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nearby, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, near the cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is the part of the town known as the Kolonjia. And that cafe was one of the alternative command posts, a place where the Vitezovi would regularly rally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And actually, that part of the town, from April on, was under their control. It was their territory, so to speak. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. One could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we said a moment ago that all lower-level units were subordinated to the command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But let us explain things and maybe the Prosecutor will ask you to elucidate other things more clearly. So we agree that the Vitezovi were the bosses there in that part of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Their number was small, and if we give them such an attribute, then certainly they had a particular assignment. They were relatively small in number compared to the overall strength of the HVO, and it is difficult to call them bosses in a given region unless they were given such a role.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you are trying to tell us that they were not feared in this particular part of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. Everyone knew that, including the HVO command and the brigades you mentioned a moment ago, those that you listed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, the command of the military police, you said you knew that it was in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it seems that the dialogue being so quick, we don't know who's asking the question and who is giving the answer. So we can't really follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kovacic, you've had nearly an hour of cross-examination. I hope you can bring things to a conclusion at least by the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will do my best, but you do understand that it is not really unimportant witness for my client, and some things seems to be different by the understanding of this witness, and I have to clarify some things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Just for your information, Your Honours, Mr. Naumovski will be rather short, because we were trying to divide, and I will certainly do my best. I already skipped some things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, bear in mind the problem of the interpretation, please, and what the Prosecutor has just said a moment ago, so that we can follow correctly the questions and the answers, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have heard. I have been reprimanded for going too quickly a moment ago in our dialogue, but the blame is mine entirely. Tell me, please, is it true that the military police, and you being a citizen who moved around quite a bit, that you knew that the military police guarded the key buildings in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. I did not have any occasion to see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For instance, wasn't the military police in front of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. The command posts where they were providing security for military establishments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we're talking about the period from April 1993 onwards, not all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: April 1993? Yes, even before that the military police did secure certain military facilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that all those security platoons come under the same military police, which had its command in the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I assume so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the cinema hall, you told us that among the military policemen you recognised somebody called Zlatko Nakic. I should like to show you his photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D51/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, regardless of the poor quality of the photograph, if you can recognise and identify this person as the person you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know that he was a member of the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apropos, did you hear later on that he was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And let us dwell for a moment on the period that you mentioned; that is, January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber, to save time, to documents D9/2, and D10/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to show you these documents, to expedite things, but very briefly, you said that there were a series of incidents in town in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You agree that efforts were made to establish control and that the police tried to do something in that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. There were attempts but no results.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the results were poor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But efforts did exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. If we view them in the context of the results, since it was possible to have some effect on the situation, one wonders whether those efforts were really appropriate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You agree that there were certain groups at the time, as a result of various circumstances, that existed in the territory of the town and who were extremists and who were the main causes of those incidents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, but their appearance or emergence was partly programmed. Rather, those units were given freedom to act as part of the local forces of the HVO, which points to the conclusion that they were units executing certain assignments according to established plans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but we agree that the most prominent were units coming from outside the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't agree, because many of the leaders of these infamous units were people from Vitez itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, Witness, did you know that in '93 the commander of the military police in Vitez of the 4th battalion of the military police was a person called Anto Sliskovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In Vitez, no, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few more words on another topic. You told us that you were a member of the committee for the protection -- I apologise. My question was wrong. I meant Pasko Ljubicic was the commander of that unit. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard of him, and I know that he was a commander in a sense of a part of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise for my error. So I was saying that you were a member of the committee for the protection of the interests of Muslims. Two brief questions: That body was operational in the second half of 1992; was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Will you please tell me what time you are referring to, time period?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From 1992 until 1993, it existed throughout, and then developed into war presidency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that committee was not formally registered anywhere as an association or anything else, according to the laws in force at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I think it was not, but I was one of the members who was not responsible for that kind of question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in spite of the climate that prevailed, nobody prevented any such body from operating. The HVO that was in power in the municipality allowed such body to operate; in fact, you were collocutors in many dialogues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, we were not collocutors, and I couldn't agree with what you just said, because, as you can see from the series of documents that you, among others, have produced, the institution of the co-ordination body does not appear as a negotiator or as a signatory, though individuals from that body did participate in social and political life, but on a different basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in any event, we agree that it was a public association, that it was a group operating in public, and that it acted to protect the interests of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, but regarding the freedom given by the HVO, that is highly questionable, and I don't agree with that, because neither did we have the premises, nor did we have any proper conditions for work, and even the members of that body were looked upon with disfavour by the HVO authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But until the very beginning of 1993, nobody prohibited the activities of that committee, and it developed into the war presidency; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the war presidency was founded by decree of the President of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Dr. Mujezinovic was elected President in the beginning of 1993. And the competencies of that war presidency, as evident from the title, was that it gave instructions to the Territorial Defence and the BiH army, of course respecting the military hierarchy in the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. Not just the BiH army. The war presidency was a form that was institutionalised through the decisions of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that is how it was formed in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was operative?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go onto another topic. On Vitez television, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted) Was it all the time under the control of the Territorial Defence or, rather, the army of the BiH? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, the relay station was at a place which is near large Muslim localities, so that one could say that it was under the control of the army, of course anyone could use it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they could cover the area, they could watch the area into that -- the programmes to that relay station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Nenad Santic again, not only at the roadblocks, but that he was in Ahmici on the 16th of April. How do you know that he was in Ahmici? Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: A large number of witnesses stated it; those who escaped, who fled to Zenica after the massacre in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But could you give us some names, or a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, right now I cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you then describe the place and time when you were told that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. It was happening in May or June '93, in Zenica, where I was living with my family at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In one of your statements to the investigators in '98, and yesterday you also mentioned it, you spoke about the name of that action in April '93, that is, 48 Hours of Ashes and Dust.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the information we learnt from people who survived that trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had some witnesses about events in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that that term became known and that you believed that that term came to be because an intelligence man of the BiH army gave it the name of the action, and that he learned about that by interviewing, by questioning HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: True, even though I did hear that term, but it didn't tell me anything. It did not mean anything to me while I was in the prison at Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you remember the name of that intelligence man from the BiH army who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That man, the intelligence man who was involved in those interviews, it was Fadil Zaninovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was he from Vitez? Zenica? Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: He was from Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned it, and I won't ask all the questions that I really should put to you about that. That man that you mentioned right now, was he Ramiz Dugalic's subordinate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't Ramiz Dugalic the one who spoke about the term, who spread that term?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I did not hear it from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Miroslav Bralo, Cicko, and you spoke about him first when he planted a bomb and killed Salkic, and then you heard about him later on, when it came to trench digging.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that Cicko Bralo, after Salkic's murder, was detained, he was detained in Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I did not hear anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said, but will you please confirm it, because I'm not sure I understood you properly, when you mentioned him the second time in relation to digging, you said that one man who was at the digging, and who was not a local, had said that there was a Cicko Bralo who boasted about being Cicko Bralo or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, a man who was imprisoned there but did not come from the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that man, who was not a local man, was affirming the identity of a man who affirmed that he was Cicko Bralo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, no, no. He was not affirming his identity. He said that one Cicko was boasting about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I mean, he did not know, he did not know the name or the nickname, nor could he repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then explained to us that a meeting, which the HVO had convened for 16th of April, was just a ruse, was simply to put the army of BiH to sleep and to catch them unawares.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown D26/2, which was tendered earlier, with Witness G. D26/2. Witness AC, will you please look at the upper left corner. It has the date and then "News." And this is the incidents commission in Vitez, and so on and so forth. So, evidently, this news is broadcast that that meeting was held, and so on and so forth. And then it is proposed that every side takes care of its own criminals, that they try to hold meetings of heads of security service centres, various initiatives, and so on and so forth. This is the announcement of the meeting, a public announcement of the meeting which was to be held on the 16th of April. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, I don't see any signatory here, so I cannot confirm your words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. This is the copy of the news read on the radio. It was just a news item on the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Let us divide it. A, was it broadcast at the television station (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I can't really confirm that, (redacted) (redacted). I did not -- I was not directly involved at that level. I did not really go through the documents and approve or refuse their broadcasting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you cannot either confirm or deny that it was broadcast?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's now eleven. Would that be a convenient moment, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us round off this topic about television, that is, the news item there. Could you confirm or deny that other radio or television stations also transmitted the same news item?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that. May I explain briefly why?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I don't think we need that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that an HVO soldier, and subsequently you said he was a member of the Vitez Brigade, on the 18th of April, on the eve of the car bomb explosion in Stari Vitez, that is, the man who was guarding the building in which you lived, told all the tenants in the building to go down to the cellar. Tell us, did you see any flashes on the soldier's uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: He had an HVO flash.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he wearing a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The uniform, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was not wearing a black uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I know him. He's from Vitez, but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he one of the Vitezovi that operated in that borough?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. I think he was a member of what I might term as the rest of the HVO. I mean, those which were not the units that you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That same day, you were detained and put in a cinema, and the man who escorted you was a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any insignia, any flash, anything that would distinguish him as a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: He belonged to the military police. They did have some flashes such as was worn by the military police at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Such as, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, the markings of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, he did have that kind of marking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us there were about 600 persons detained in the cinema.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to tell you that witness Hendrik Morsink said here that there were, and that is day 71, first day of the transcript, line 20, he said: "I remember, and I think that in the cinema basement," so this is a building housing the Vitez headquarters, "where we saw about 70 male detainees, all wearing civilian clothes." So this figure is very different.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, that cannot be correct. When I mentioned the figure, when I said "several hundred, as many as 600," I meant three places where the detained Bosniaks were, so the cinema hall, the SDK, and the chess club.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in the cinema itself you would agree that there were about 70 of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In the cinema, no. No way. There were many more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But not 600.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I could not count them. Nobody cared about counting at the time. That figure is the result of analysis of the number of precincts and the knowledge of how many of us were in each of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. But you will agree that only men were detained in the cinema?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were all of military age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: By and large but not only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you remember that a few days later a number of people were released, some 20 of them, because of health problems. You know that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, there were some cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will agree that people were released individually for health reasons and other, and then a large-ish group was released exclusively on health grounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, as you started, it will turn out that we were all ill, but I would not agree that they were all released for health reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I wasn't clear enough. A group of about 20 was released for health reasons only?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, I confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And tell us as regards the conditions there. And we also heard it from other witnesses, including Mr. Morsink. Contact with families as allowed, and they brought food and other things. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, one could say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was a medical commission which visited the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. Not in those precincts where I was kept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I could not confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think they came to visit them, but I can't affirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But are you aware that there was a certain number of people -- we do not know the exact number -- who came themselves there for their personal safety?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I doubt that, because why didn't they stay there after others had been released? All of who were there were taken in by force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But wouldn't we agree that chaos reigned in the town at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In the town itself, maybe not. If it did, the HVO units were in the town, so they would be directly responsible for any chaos that there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. In a way, you told us that the detainees in the cinema were there to protect the command in the hotel itself. I am going to ask you now [in English] to put on ELMO a photo, tender it under Z2186. [Interpretation] Witness, you know Vitez very well, so when we get the photograph, I would like to ask you to take a look at it on the monitor. Yes, that's it. If you look at the bottom -- [in English] I would kindly ask the -- yes, that will do. Great. Thank you. [Interpretation] In the bottom left-hand corner we see three buildings marked A, B and C. Can you identify the A building as the hotel that we spoke about, which was where the command of the operative zone was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I know Vitez well, but looking at it from this angle, it's a little -- it looks a little strange, and I cannot say with any certainty whether that is the building you asked about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at building C, above the first building, and if I tell you that that is the post office building, is it --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, it corresponds to the geometric distribution of the buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I were to draw your attention to the building to the right of the hotel marked B, is that the Worker's University where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: A part of it, yes, but in this compound there is another part of the premises which should be somewhere in between A and B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at it closely, it's not a very good photograph, I know, Witness, but if you take a careful look at the B, it is right beside the rear of the T-shaped building, and in front you can see the building that you have been talking about, the front of the building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, geometrically speaking, then, it does reflect the position of the buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is about 150 metres between these two buildings, between building A and B?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, if you calculate the distance from A to B, but you could have moved the A to the other end of the building, and then you would see that the distance is much smaller.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but from the photograph we see the ratio. It's not as great a distance as you just said. Thank you. Tell me, please, if the detainees were there to form a sort of protection or shield, why was that? Were there any artillery attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, there were artillery attacks after the killing in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the town was shelled, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And houses were destroyed in the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even civilian buildings; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the health centre as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The health centre was in the immediate vicinity. I did not move around in that area, so I cannot confirm whether the health centre was hit and destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Let us go back to the question of the detention. And be as brief as possible in your answers, if you will. You said that from the house to the cinema you were escorted by a military policeman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The cinema was protected by the military policeman, was it not? From the cinema to the chess club you were transferred by the military police, were you not, with the group? And the chess club was also guarded by the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the chess club, you were taken to Kaonik, once again transported by the military police, escorted by the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were transferred back to the cinema once again by the military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You have already told us that (redacted) in Kaonik was beaten by the guards. Did he say that the military policeman, Petrovic Zarko, hit him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I didn't catch the name. Would you repeat the name?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zarko Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When released from the cinema, you mentioned a moment ago that you talked to Santic. Let me remind you, Witness. You were then given the possibility of choosing. You were offered, and we heard that some of you were prevailed upon to remain in Vitez, or you were given the choice of leaving Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you signed your particular choice and said, "I am going," the other person said he wasn't going, and so on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was 16 individuals in all, were there not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: About that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Santic try to influence people and prevail upon them to stay, saying that matters would become normalised there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: There were attempts of that kind, yes, but we thought that this was a hypocritical offer, in view of the fact of what had happened in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't believe it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: And the accused Cerkez also made a statement within that context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. I would like to refer, for the purposes of the Court, to document D28/2. That is the statement, D28/2. It was introduced earlier on. I am now going to ask you to take a look at the following document [in English] D28/1, which was just tendered by the Prosecution. [Interpretation] You saw the document a moment ago. Let me ask you first, you were not a member of the military units of the BiH army when you were taken into custody; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The title of the document says that it is a list of prisoners of war? You were a civilian detainee, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I was mobilised as a military conscript and my task was, (redacted) (redacted) So I cannot use that attribute in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you were arrested, you were no longer a member (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, I worked in (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you want to say is that your status was not quite clear cut; that is to say, whether you were a civilian or whether you were a military man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, it was quite clear, because I had multiple duties to attend to; some of them were of a civilian nature, others were of a military nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You notice that in the document there was some entries written by hand. Have you got an explanation for those hand-written remarks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I didn't write the document, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some of them have been written in English.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AC [RESUMED]
